item.title: Horizon Europe Proposal Template RIA: 40-Page Section Map
item.dc:creator: Aoba Works
item.description: Horizon Europe proposal template RIA (2026-27): the 40-page Part B limit, pages per section, RIA vs IA vs CSA differences and the Portal download steps.
item.content:encoded:
How this guide was made: drafted with AI assistance from the official sources linked below, then passed an automated editorial check before publishing. Our process

For 2026-2027 calls, the Horizon Europe proposal template for a RIA is the "Standard Application Form (HE RIA, IA)". Its Part B has a hard limit of 40 pages, or 45 pages when the topic uses lump sum funding (NCP Flanders). Part B has three scored sections: 1 Excellence, 2 Impact and 3 Quality and efficiency of the implementation. The template suggests about 18 pages for Excellence, 6 for Impact and 15 for Implementation (criteri.ai summary of the template). Innovation Actions (IA) use the same file. Coordination and Support Actions (CSA) use a shorter template with a 25-page limit.

Which option is right for you?

The right starting point depends on your call type and on whether you are reusing an older proposal.

Your situationWhat to pick firstFirst page to open
First-time RIA applicant (university lab, SME, NGO)The 2026-27 RIA/IA template linked from your topic, plus your PICTopic page > "Topic conditions and documents" on the Funding & Tenders Portal, then /eu-funding-and-tenders-portal-registration-pic-in-6-steps/
Consultant or grants office reusing a 2024-25 proposalA fresh copy of the v5.x template. Don't paste into the old 45-page file"Download Part B templates" inside the Submission System
IA (closer to market, TRL 6-8 work)The same RIA/IA template, with extra weight on Section 2General Annexes 2026-20278493_15/090166e526657ddd)
CSA (networking, coordination, policy support)The separate HE CSA template (25 pages)HE CSA template PDF
Two-stage call, stage 1The stage 1 template (10 pages, Excellence and Impact only)/horizon-hlth-2027-02-tool-01-two-stage-dates-page-limits/
EIC PathfinderThe EIC-specific template, not the RIA one/eic-pathfinder-2026-deadlines-3-challenges-7-steps/
Tight budget, no consultantYour National Contact Point (free) plus the official templateHorizon Europe NCP Portal

What Is the Official RIA Proposal Template?

The official RIA proposal template is the Commission's "Standard Application Form (HE RIA, IA)". You download it from your call topic on the Funding & Tenders Portal. It is set up so evaluators can score your proposal against Excellence, Impact and Implementation.

A Horizon Europe application has two parts. Part A is a set of web forms in the Submission System: participants, budget, and the ethics and security self-assessments. Part B is the technical description you write and upload as a PDF. The Commission publishes the generic RIA/IA template as a PDF in its reference documents. Inside the Submission System you get an editable RTF version that matches your call (Portal IT How To: Proposal forms).

The version matters. For the 2026-2027 Work Programme, the Commission released a revised form in December 2025 (NCP Flanders reported it on 19 December 2025). It made four changes (NCP Flanders):

  • RIA/IA page limit cut from 45 to 40 pages (lump sum: from 50 to 45)
  • CSA page limit cut from 30 to 25 pages (lump sum: from 33 to 28)
  • Section 2.1 simplified, and the "scale and significance" guidance removed
  • In Section 3.1, the "other cost categories" and "in-kind contributions" tables removed, and the purchase costs table simplified

Secondary summaries cite different version numbers and dates for this release, including "v5.0", "v5.1 (22 January 2026)" and "Version 10.0, 15 December 2025" (criteri.ai, Accelopment, Europa Media Trainings). Don't rely on any of those labels. Use the template linked from your topic's Submission System, because that is the one the page-limit check runs against.

If you want to know how each section maps to the evaluator's score sheet, see our Horizon Europe Part B scoring map.

RIA vs IA vs CSA Template: What's the Difference?

RIA and IA use the same Part B template and the same 40-page limit. The CSA template is shorter (25 pages), and its Excellence criterion asks about the quality of your coordination and support measures, not about going beyond the state of the art.

FeatureRIAIACSA
Template fileStandard Application Form (HE RIA, IA)Same file as RIAStandard Application Form (HE CSA)
Part B limit (standard)40 pages40 pages25 pages
Part B limit (lump sum)45 pages45 pages28 pages
Excellence focusObjectives, ambition beyond state of the art, methodologySame, usually with higher TRL targetsQuality of coordination/support measures and methodology
Impact weight when ranking1.01.51.0
Typical funding rate100%70% (100% for non-profit entities)100%
Section 3.1 tables3.1a–3.1h3.1a–3.1hSame work plan logic, shorter

Sources for the table: page limits from NCP Flanders; IA weighting, thresholds and funding rates from the Horizon Europe 2026-2027 General Annexes8493_15/090166e526657ddd); CSA criterion wording as summarised by Proposia.

What this means in practice:

  • RIA: Excellence is where most proposals win or lose. Methodology gets the biggest page budget (about 14 pages).
  • IA: you write the same sections, but Impact counts 1.5× when proposals are ranked. Give Section 2.2 a credible exploitation and commercialisation route.
  • CSA: there is no research methodology to defend. The space goes to how you will coordinate, network, run events or support policy. Evaluators still expect a short note on context and existing initiatives (Proposia).

For all three types, you must score at least 3 out of 5 on each criterion and at least 10 out of 15 overall, unless the work programme sets different thresholds (General Annexes8493_15/090166e526657ddd)).

How Many Pages Is the Part B Template?

A RIA Part B for 2026-2027 calls may be 40 pages at most, or 45 pages if the topic uses lump sum funding. The count includes the cover/title and participant list plus Sections 1-3, with every table, figure and reference inside them (criteri.ai, Proposia).

These are the recommended per-section allocations for a standard (non-lump-sum) RIA/IA, as of October 2026. They are guidance, not separate hard caps. Only the total is enforced.

Part B elementRecommended pages (standard)Lump sumChange vs 2024-25 template
Title page and list of participants11—
1.1 Objectives and ambition44—
1.2 Methodology1414—
2.1 Project's pathways towards impact33was 4
2.2 Measures to maximise impact + 2.3 Summary3 (combined)3was 5; 2.3 now optional
3.1 Work plan and resources (incl. tables)1217was 14 / 19
3.2 Capacity of participants and consortium33—
Total4045was 45 / 50

Sources: criteri.ai and Accelopment.

Other limits you may run into:

  • Two-stage calls, stage 1: 10 pages (Europa Media Trainings).
  • CSA: 25 pages, or 28 with lump sum (NCP Flanders).
  • Programme Co-fund: 65 pages (criteri.ai).
  • EIC Pathfinder 2026: 22 pages for Open, 30 for Challenges (EU-Büro NCP).

Sections 4 and 5 (ethics and security) don't eat into the 40 pages. Those self-assessments are now completed in Part A web forms (Proposia).

The Submission System enforces the limit itself. If you upload a file that is too long, you can still submit, but the excess pages get a watermark and a warning tells you they will be dismissed in evaluation (Portal IT How To). After the deadline those pages become invisible to the experts (criteri.ai).

What Goes in Section 1 (Excellence)?

Section 1 covers objectives and ambition (1.1, about 4 pages) and methodology (1.2, about 14 pages). Together that is roughly 18 of your 40 pages.

1.1 Objectives and ambition should state measurable, achievable objectives that clearly match the topic text. It explains how you go beyond the state of the art and gives the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) at the start and end of the project where relevant. The template also asks you to name the ground-breaking element if there is one (Proposia).

1.2 Methodology covers the following (Proposia):

  • concepts, models and assumptions, plus the main challenges and how you will handle them
  • links to other national or EU R&I activities (around 1 page)
  • why an interdisciplinary approach is needed (around half a page)
  • social sciences and humanities (SSH) integration where the topic requires it
  • the sex and gender dimension in the research content (mandatory unless the topic exempts it)
  • open science practices and research data management under FAIR principles; open access to publications is mandatory

How to draft Section 1:

  1. Copy the "Expected outcomes" and "Scope" bullets from your topic page into a scratch file.
  2. Write one objective for each outcome, each with a measurable target. Example (illustrative only): "Reduce sensor drift to below 2% over 1,000 hours, validated in a relevant environment (TRL 5) by month 30."
  3. State the start and end TRL for each technology strand.
  4. In 1.2, follow the template's sub-headings in order so evaluators can tick off each element.
  5. Write the gender and open science paragraphs about your research. Generic policy text doesn't count.
  6. Check the length. If 1.2 goes past about 14 pages, the extra space has to come out of Section 3, which is already tight.

What Goes in Section 2 (Impact)?

Section 2 asks how your results lead to the topic's expected outcomes (2.1) and what you will do to make that happen: dissemination, exploitation, IP and communication (2.2). The recommended budget is about 6 pages in total.

2.1 Project's pathways towards impact (about 3 pages) links your results to the expected outcomes in the topic and to the wider impacts of the work programme destination. The 2026-27 template removed the guidance on describing the "scale and significance" of your contribution. The Commission said those measures were complex and often hard to quantify (NCP Flanders). The focus is now on who benefits, how and why (Future Needs). Also cover requirements and barriers outside your control, such as regulation or market uptake. Risks to delivering the project belong in Section 3 (Proposia).

2.2 Measures to maximise impact (shares about 3 pages with 2.3) is a first version of your plan for dissemination, exploitation and communication. It must include your IP strategy and name target groups for each measure (Proposia). This is an admissibility issue: the General Annexes require a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication, at proposal stage unless the call says otherwise (General Annexes8493_15/090166e526657ddd)).

2.3 Summary (the "key elements of the impact section" canvas) is now optional (Accelopment). If space is tight, drop it before you cut content from 2.2.

How to draft Section 2:

  1. Make a three-column list: each expected outcome from the topic, the project result that feeds it, and the group that uses that result.
  2. Turn each row into a short pathway paragraph for 2.1.
  3. In 2.2, give each measure a target group, a channel and a timing. Example (illustrative): "Open-source toolkit released on a public repository at M24, targeted at regional grid operators via the partner's user group."
  4. For an IA, add the commercialisation route (who sells or deploys, and when). Impact is weighted 1.5 in IA ranking.

What Goes in Section 3 (Implementation)?

Section 3 contains the work plan and resources (3.1, about 12 pages including the mandatory tables, or 17 with lump sum) and the capacity of the consortium (3.2, about 3 pages).

3.1 Work plan and resources starts with a short narrative and a graphical overview of how the work packages fit together and when they run, for example a Gantt chart (RIA/IA template). Then come the tables:

TableContent
3.1aList of work packages
3.1bWork package descriptions
3.1cList of deliverables
3.1dList of milestones
3.1eCritical risks for implementation
3.1fSummary of staff effort
3.1gSubcontracting costs
3.1hPurchase costs (major equipment)

Tables 3.1i (other cost categories) and 3.1j (in-kind contributions) were removed in the 2026-27 version (Accelopment). The Commission's reason was that evaluators mainly need high-level information on the work plan, and more detail can be requested after selection (NCP Flanders).

In lump sum topics, 3.1 gets 17 pages because each work package needs enough detail to justify its share of the lump sum (criteri.ai).

3.2 Capacity of participants and consortium as a whole explains why these partners, with this expertise and these facilities, can deliver. Show complementarity, a clear role for each partner, and industry involvement where exploitation depends on it. Evaluators comment negatively on unexplained imbalances in effort and on partners whose role isn't clear (Proposia).

How to draft Section 3:

  1. Fix the work package list and the person-months per partner in a spreadsheet first.
  2. Enter the same figures in the Part A budget and in Tables 3.1a, 3.1b and 3.1f.
  3. Plan the Data Management Plan and the dissemination, exploitation and communication plan as early deliverables. Proposia notes these are expected by month 6 (Proposia).
  4. Include a project management work package.
  5. Write 3.2 last, once roles are final.

How to Format Tables for Work Packages and Deliverables?

Use the template's tables as they are, keep the columns in order, and make sure the numbers match Part A exactly. The fonts used in tables count toward the formatting rules too.

These are the expected columns, as summarised by Proposia from the template:

TableColumns to keep
3.1a Work packagesWP number, WP title, lead participant number, lead participant short name, person-months, start month, end month
3.1b WP descriptionWP number, title, objectives, tasks with task leads and participant roles
3.1c DeliverablesDeliverable number (e.g. D2.1), name, short description, WP number, lead participant, type, dissemination level, delivery month
3.1d MilestonesMilestone number, name, related WP(s), due month, means of verification
3.1e Critical risksRisk description, likelihood/severity, WP(s) involved, mitigation measures
3.1f Staff effortParticipants × WPs matrix of person-months, with totals
3.1g SubcontractingParticipant, cost (EUR), description and justification of tasks
3.1h Purchase costsParticipant, cost (EUR), justification where purchase costs exceed 15% of personnel costs

The 15% trigger for justifying purchase costs comes from the 2026-27 summaries (Accelopment, Proposia). Check the exact wording in the template version for your topic.

Pitfalls and fixes:

  • Person-months don't match across 3.1a, 3.1b, 3.1f and the Part A budget. Fix: generate all four from one spreadsheet and check them again after every budget change.
  • Shrinking table fonts to save space. The minimum 11-point rule also applies to text in tables, and using narrow fonts to get around the limit is treated as a breach (criteri.ai).
  • Pasting tables as images. Graphics may be at most 300 dpi (Portal IT How To), and scanned tables are hard to read. Keep tables as text.
  • Deliverable months outside the WP's start/end range. Fix: sort 3.1c by WP and compare each date with 3.1a.

Where Do I Download the Official RIA Template?

Download it from your call topic on the Funding & Tenders Portal. The generic PDF is there for reading, and the editable RTF is in the Submission System via "Download Part B templates".

Steps (Portal labels as of October 2026):

  1. Go to the Funding & Tenders Portal and search for your topic ID (e.g. HORIZON-CL5-2027-…).
  2. On the topic page, open "Topic conditions and documents" and find the application form link, "Standard application form (HE RIA, IA)". This opens the generic template (PDF). Use it to plan the structure.
  3. Click "Start submission". You need an EU Login account and your organisation's PIC (Funding & Tenders Portal Online Manual). If you don't have one yet, see /eu-funding-and-tenders-portal-registration-pic-in-6-steps/.
  4. In the Submission System, click "Download Part B templates". You get the call-specific templates as editable RTF files (Portal IT How To).
  5. Write in that file. When you're done, export to PDF and upload it under "Part B and Annexes" with "Upload". The PDF must not be locked, encrypted, password-protected or digitally signed. File names may only contain Latin letters, numbers, dots, dashes, underscores and spaces (Portal IT How To).
  6. Click "Validate", fix any errors, then click "Submit". You can resubmit as often as you like before the deadline (Funding & Tenders Portal Online Manual). Check the result in My Proposals.

To compare templates across action types, the CSA form is published as a separate PDF.

What Are Common Mistakes When Filling the RIA Template?

The most expensive mistakes are going over the page limit, using an outdated template, and having Part B figures that don't match Part A. All three are avoidable.

  1. Writing in the 2024-25 template. An old file was built for 45 pages. Under the 2026-27 rules, anything past page 40 is watermarked and then hidden from evaluators (criteri.ai). Fix: start from the RTF in your topic's Submission System and move your text into it.
  2. Ignoring the formatting floor. The template requires Times New Roman (or Times / Nimbus Roman No. 9 L) at 11 pt minimum, single line spacing, A4 pages and 15 mm margins (criteri.ai, Proposia). Fix: set up styles once and don't override them locally.
  3. Leaving instruction text in place. The italic guidance in the template uses pages that count toward your limit. Fix: delete every instruction block before exporting, and keep only the headings.
  4. Mismatched effort and budget. Example (illustrative): Table 3.1f shows 48 person-months for a partner, but Part A budgets 36. Evaluators read that as weak planning. Fix: use one source spreadsheet.
  5. Missing the dissemination and exploitation plan. It's an admissibility requirement (General Annexes8493_15/090166e526657ddd)). Fix: write a real 2.2, even if it's short.
  6. Skipping call-specific additions. Some topics add requirements, for example lump sum work package detail, blind evaluation at stage 1 (Proposia) or extra sub-sections. Fix: read the topic's "Topic conditions and documents" section before you write a single section.
  7. Uploading at the last minute. Technical problems close to the deadline are hard to fix. Fix: submit a complete draft days ahead, then resubmit. If the system blocks you, open a ticket right away. See our helpdesk guide.

Next steps

You can get the template structure right today. If you want help, the free option is your National Contact Point, and paid training or consultants are available too.

Do it yourself today:

  1. Open your topic page, click "Start submission", and use "Download Part B templates" to get the current RTF.
  2. Paste the per-section page budget table above into the top of your draft as a working note (delete it before export). Assign an owner to each section.
  3. Build one spreadsheet for WPs, person-months and deliverables, and fill Tables 3.1a–3.1f from it.

If you'd rather not do it alone:

  • National Contact Points (NCPs): a free, publicly funded service in each EU Member State and Associated Country. They can review your structure and explain the call rules (Horizon Europe NCP Portal). They suit first-time applicants and small teams. They're less suited if you want someone to write the proposal: NCPs advise but don't draft.
  • Paid proposal-writing courses, for example those listed by Europa Media Trainings. Prices are set per course (as of October 2026; check the official page). They suit grant officers who will write several proposals. They're less suited if you have one deadline in the next two weeks, because the course won't write your text.
  • Private grant consultants: fees and models vary (fixed fee, success fee or both), so read the contract carefully. This suits SMEs with no in-house grant writer. It's not a good fit if you need to own and defend the scientific content yourself. One limitation: no consultant can change how the evaluation is done or what it decides.

Related guides on this site:

  • Horizon Europe Part B: 2026 Scoring Map

  • Horizon Europe Health Calls 2027: Topics, Dates, Budgets

FAQ

Is the RIA template the same for all Horizon Europe clusters?

Yes. All clusters use the same Standard Application Form (HE RIA, IA) with the same 40-page limit (45 with lump sum) for 2026-2027 calls (NCP Flanders). Individual topics can still add conditions, such as lump sum detail or two-stage rules. Always use the version linked from your topic.

Can I add extra sections to the standard RIA template?

You shouldn't change the numbered structure, because evaluators score against those headings. You can add sub-headings, figures and tables inside the sections, but everything counts toward the page limit. Annexes are only allowed where the call asks for them.

What font and margin rules apply to the Part B template?

The minimum is Times New Roman (or an equivalent such as Times or Nimbus Roman No. 9 L) at 11 points, with single line spacing, A4 pages and 15 mm margins (criteri.ai, Proposia). The rule also applies to text inside tables. Using narrow fonts to fit more text counts as a breach.

Do Pathfinder or EIC calls use a different template?

Yes. EIC Pathfinder has its own application form. For 2026, Part B is limited to 22 pages for Pathfinder Open and 30 pages for Pathfinder Challenges (EU-Büro NCP). EIC Accelerator also uses its own process. See our EIC Accelerator deadlines guide.

item.title: EU Funding and Tenders Portal Helpdesk: Ticket in 5 Steps
item.dc:creator: Aoba Works
item.description: How to use the EU Funding and Tenders Portal helpdesk: open an IT ticket in 5 steps, what to include, response times, and when to call your NCP instead.
item.content:encoded:
How this guide was made: drafted with AI assistance from the official sources linked below, then passed an automated editorial check before publishing. Our process

The EU Funding and Tenders Portal helpdesk is the IT Helpdesk. You contact it through an online contact form, which you find under Guidance & documents > Helpdesk & support > IT Helpdesk. You can also reach it from your user icon once you are logged in. It handles technical problems with portal tools such as submission, registration and EU Login. Questions about eligibility or what to write in a proposal go to a different service: the Research Enquiry Service, or your National Contact Point (NCP) for Horizon Europe (Online Manual – Help). If a submission fails because of a fault on the portal's side, you have 4 calendar days after the call closes to file a complaint through the same form (Complaints about failed submission).

Which option is right for you?

The right helpdesk depends on whether your problem is technical, legal/administrative or about content. This table matches common situations to the service to contact first.

Your situationWhat to pick firstFirst page to open
Beginner who can't log in, can't find the "Submit" button, or sees an error messageIT Helpdesk ticketIT Helpdesk contact form
Your organisation has no PIC yet and you have a legal question about validation or appointing a LEARParticipant Validation HelpdeskValidation form
Your organisation already has a PIC and validation has asked for documentsMessages tab in Manage my OrganisationsRegister an organisation (IT How To)
Daily work: a grant consultant or research office asking a Horizon Europe legal/financial questionResearch Enquiry ServiceR&I Contact us
Tight budget, first proposal, you need help on eligibility or fit in your own languageNational Contact Point (free)NCP directory
A question about one specific call (not Horizon Europe)The functional mailbox named in the call documentsCall topic page, "Topic conditions and documents"
A general question about the EUEurope DirectOnline Manual – Help

Here is the reason behind each pick. IT staff can see system logs but won't judge whether you are eligible. NCPs give free advice in your own language but cannot fix the portal. Validation staff deal with your organisation's legal data, not with your proposal.

What is the EU Funding and Tenders Portal Helpdesk?

The EU Funding and Tenders Portal Helpdesk is the IT Helpdesk "for IT-related questions" about the portal's tools and processes. The Online Manual lists it next to separate services for validation, Horizon Europe enquiries and general EU questions (Online Manual – Help).

The portal's Help page lists four routes:

  • IT Helpdesk: for IT-related questions, reached through the contact form.
  • Participant Validation Helpdesk: "for legal questions relating to participant validation and LEAR appointment if you have NOT registered an organisation yet". Organisations that are already registered use the messaging feature in Manage my Organisations instead.
  • Research Enquiry Service or your National Contact Point: for Horizon Europe questions.
  • Europe Direct: for general questions about the EU. Programme-specific questions go to the functional mailbox given in the call documents.

(All four routes are from the Online Manual – Help, as of October 2026.)

The IT Helpdesk staff work Monday to Friday during Central European Time working hours (SEP user manual mirror). Plan around that. If you open a ticket on Friday evening for a Monday deadline, nobody will read it on Saturday or Sunday.

Pitfall: people treat "helpdesk" as a single inbox. If you ask the IT Helpdesk whether your startup counts as an SME, or whether a cost is eligible, you will usually be sent somewhere else, and that costs you days. Work out which kind of question you have before you write. For sorting out the SME question itself, see EU Funding for SMEs: 7 Open 2026 Calls and How to Qualify.

How to submit a ticket to the EU Funding and Tenders Portal Helpdesk

Log in to the portal, open Guidance & documents > Helpdesk & support, click IT Helpdesk, choose the right domain, describe the problem and send it. The five steps below follow the labels used in the official IT How To pages.

  1. Log in with EU Login. Sign in at the Funding & Tenders Portal. If two-step verification is what's blocking you, try the fixes in EU Funding and Tenders Portal Two Factor Authentication 2026 before you write a ticket.
  2. Open the helpdesk page. From the top menu choose Guidance & documents, then Helpdesk & support, then click the IT Helpdesk icon. The Register an organisation guide describes exactly this path. If you are already logged in, the SEP manual also documents a shortcut: User icon > IT Helpdesk at the top right (SEP user manual mirror).
  3. Select the domain. For problems with the proposal submission system, the official instruction is to select the domain Submission of proposals (Submit a proposal – IT How To). Pick whichever domain matches where the error happened (registration, grant management and so on). A wrong domain can delay routing.
  4. Describe the problem and attach evidence. Enter "the details of the problem" in the form (Register an organisation) and attach a screenshot if you need to (SEP user manual mirror). The next section lists what to include.
  5. Submit and keep the reference. Send the form and save the acknowledgement or ticket number. Quote it in every follow-up message, and in any later complaint about a failed submission.

Example (illustrative): a university research office sees an error when it clicks Submit on a Horizon Europe proposal. It selects Submission of proposals, pastes the exact error text, attaches a screenshot showing the system clock, and gives the proposal ID and call identifier. That one message lets the helpdesk find the session in its logs without asking for anything more.

What information do you need to fill in the helpdesk ticket form?

You need the right domain, a precise description, the identifiers for your proposal or organisation, and a screenshot. The official pages confirm the domain selection, the free-text problem details and the screenshot attachment. The other items in the table are a checklist so the helpdesk doesn't have to write back to you.

ScreenshotAttachmentYes, "if required" (SEP manual mirror)PNG of the error with the clock visible

Browser, version, operating systemDescriptionRecommendedFirefox 131, Windows 11
Timestamp and time zoneDescriptionRecommended2026-10-24 10:42 CET
Deadline date and timeDescriptionRecommendedCloses 2026-10-28 17:00 Brussels time

Write the description in this order: what you were doing, what you expected, what happened instead, and what you have already tried. For example: "Uploading Part B (PDF) in step 5 of the submission wizard. Expected the upload to complete. Got 'File could not be uploaded' three times. Tried Chrome and Firefox and cleared the cache."

Pitfalls and fixes

  • Vague subject lines like "Urgent!!" or "Portal not working". Fix: put the deadline and the proposal ID in the first line of the description.
  • Screenshots that hide the URL bar or clock. Fix: capture the full window. If you later file a complaint, you'll need these screenshots as proof of the failure (Complaints about failed submission).
  • Sharing your password. Your EU Login username and password are personal, and the manual says not to share them with anyone (Online Manual – EU Login). Never put them in a ticket.

How long does the EU Funding and Tenders Portal Helpdesk take to respond?

The portal pages reviewed for this guide publish no general response-time commitment for ordinary IT tickets. The one written timing is for failed-submission complaints, which get an acknowledgement "the same or next working day" (Complaints about failed submission, as of October 2026).

What the official sources do say:

  • Hours: Monday to Friday, during working hours CET (SEP user manual mirror). Weekends and EU public holidays are not covered.
  • Complaints: an acknowledgement the same or next working day. EU services then check the application and access log files, and tell you the outcome "as soon as possible" (Complaints about failed submission).
  • Submission timing advice: submit "at least 48 hours before the deadline" so you avoid problems with system requirements, local configuration settings and system congestion (Electronic proposal submission).

Read those three facts together. The portal assumes you'll have about two working days to spare if something breaks. If you open a ticket 6 hours before the deadline, you are relying on someone picking it up the same afternoon.

Pitfall: treating a ticket as a deadline extension. Opening a ticket doesn't stop the clock. The Submit a proposal guide says no changes are allowed once the closure date is reached. Keep trying alternatives (another browser, another network, a colleague's machine with their own login if they have a role on the proposal) while you wait for a reply.

IT Helpdesk vs National Contact Point: which one to contact

Contact the IT Helpdesk when the portal itself fails. Contact your NCP when you need advice on eligibility, fit or proposal content. NCPs are national structures that give "guidance, practical information and assistance on all aspects of participating in Horizon Europe" (R&I Contact us).

QuestionIT HelpdeskNational Contact PointResearch Enquiry Service
"Submit button returns an error"YesNoNo
"EU Login / 2FA won't accept my code"Yes (after the EU Login help FAQ)NoNo
"Is my NGO eligible for this topic?"NoYesYes
"Does my idea fit this call and expected outcomes?"NoYes, informal feedbackLimited
"How are personnel costs calculated?"NoYesYes
LanguageEnglishUsually your national languageEU languages
CostFreeFreeFree
Who it is not forContent or strategy questionsFixing system bugs, writing your proposal for youUrgent same-day technical fixes

NCPs exist in EU Member States and in countries associated with Horizon Europe. You find yours by country and theme in the NCP directory. Some NCP information is visible without logging in, and the rest only after login (UFUK Avrupa portal guide). One limitation: NCPs only cover Horizon Europe (and related programmes in some countries). For calls under other programmes, such as Digital Europe or LIFE, check the call documents for the right contact.

The Research Enquiry Service is the Commission-level alternative. It covers questions "about research in Europe, Horizon 2020 or other research programmes and funding instruments" (R&I Contact us). National agencies such as Austria's FFG send legal and financial Horizon Europe questions there (FFG).

Example (illustrative): a Spanish startup preparing an EIC application can't tell whether its pitch deck upload failed or was never needed. The upload error goes to the IT Helpdesk. The question "is a pitch deck required at this stage?" goes to the NCP, and the call documents answer it too. Dates for that programme are in EIC Accelerator Deadlines: 2026 Cut-Off Dates and Steps.

When should you escalate a helpdesk ticket?

Escalate when the problem blocks submission, the deadline is close, and you have had no useful answer. If the call has already closed and the portal was at fault, escalate by filing a formal failed-submission complaint within 4 calendar days.

The documentation reviewed here describes no "urgent" button or priority flag. In practice, escalating means adding information to the same ticket and, after closure, switching to the formal complaint route:

  1. Reply on the same ticket. Don't open a duplicate. Quote the original reference and add new facts: a new error text, a second browser tested, how many hours are left before the deadline.
  2. Name the deadline in the first line. For example: "Call closes 2026-10-28 17:00 Brussels time. Submission blocked."
  3. Keep preparing. Save timestamped PDFs of Part B and the annexes. File attributes that show when each file was created and last modified are what the complaint procedure asks for (Complaints about failed submission).
  4. After closure, file a complaint through the IT Helpdesk within 4 calendar days, with screenshots and the timestamped files. If the complaint is upheld, the files you supplied become your proposal for evaluation. If you supplied no files, the last version recorded in the system is used.
  5. Ask the right people in parallel. If the block is really a validation issue (for example a PIC that can't be attached), use the Messages tab in your organisation's record. If it's a programme question, contact the call's functional mailbox. Both are listed in the Online Manual – Help.

Pitfalls

  • Escalating a problem on your side. Complaints are checked against IT logs to confirm "technical problems on the Portal side". A slow office network or a corrupted PDF won't count.
  • Missing the 4-day window. Calendar days include weekends. If a call closes on Thursday, the window ends on Monday.
  • Asking an NCP to escalate a bug. NCPs can advise you, but they don't run the submission system.

Common errors reported to the EU Portal Helpdesk and how to fix them

Most tickets involve EU Login and two-step verification, PIC or LEAR validation, upload or submission errors near the deadline, and confusion about proposal status. Several of these can be fixed before you write a ticket.

EU Login and two-step verification. Lost phones, codes that are rejected and locked accounts are the most common blockers. Start with the official EU Login help FAQ. Two-step verification can be requested when you start a proposal or open drafts (Submit a proposal – IT How To), so set it up days in advance. Our two-factor authentication guide covers the setup.

PIC and LEAR problems. If your organisation hasn't registered yet, legal questions about validation go to the Participant Validation Helpdesk form, not to IT. Once you have a PIC, talk to the validation team through the Messages tab of your Organisation Data Update screen (Register an organisation). If a form crashes during registration, that is an IT ticket. The full registration flow is in EU Funding and Tenders Portal Registration: PIC in 6 Steps.

Upload and submission errors. The manual names three causes: system requirements, local configuration settings and system congestion. Before you open a ticket:

  • Try a second supported browser and switch off extensions.
  • Re-export the PDF. Flatten forms and remove encryption or passwords.
  • Check the page limits and file formats in the call's templates.
  • Submit early and resubmit if you need to. "Every submitted version will replace the previous one" (Electronic proposal submission).

Page-limit problems often surface only at the last validation step. Horizon Europe Proposal Template Part B: 2026 Scoring Map shows where the limits apply.

"Did it actually submit?" Many tickets are really status questions. Check the proposal's status in My Proposals before you write. Our My Proposals status table explains what each status means.

Pitfall: sending one ticket that mixes several problems, for example "my 2FA fails and also is my budget eligible?" Split it. Send the technical part to IT and the rest to the NCP or RES.

What to do if the portal is down near a submission deadline

Record the failure with screenshots and timestamps, open an IT Helpdesk ticket that states the deadline, keep retrying, and watch for an official extension. If the call closes before you get through, file a complaint within 4 calendar days.

  1. Capture evidence straight away. Take full-screen screenshots with the time visible and note the exact error text. The complaint procedure names screenshots as proof of the failure (Complaints about failed submission).
  2. Freeze your files. Save the final Part B and annexes as PDFs before the deadline and don't edit them afterwards. The created and modified timestamps are your evidence.
  3. Open the ticket under Submission of proposals, with the proposal ID, call identifier and deadline in the first line.
  4. Retry from a different setup. Use another browser, another network, or another team member who has a role on the proposal. You can resubmit as many times as you like before closure.
  5. Watch for official notices. Check the call's topic page and the programme's news channels. The Commission has extended deadlines after portal failures before. For example, in May 2021 the EIC Pathfinder Open deadline was moved to 25 May 2021 at 17:00 CET after submission problems (ChatEIC report). Don't count on an extension. It is an exception, not a rule.
  6. After closure, complain within 4 calendar days if the portal was at fault, attaching your evidence. You'll get an acknowledgement the same or next working day.

Pitfall: waiting for an outage notice before you act. Document and submit tickets as it happens, because evidence gathered afterwards is weaker. And because the manual recommends submitting at least 48 hours early, a last-hour outage is the case where a complaint has the best chance. A problem on your own side does not qualify.

Next steps

You can sort out most helpdesk issues yourself today with three actions, and free official advisers cover most of the rest.

Do this today (DIY):

  1. Bookmark the IT Helpdesk contact form. Save a ticket template in your notes containing your PIC, EU Login e-mail and the proposal ID and call identifier, so you can paste it in seconds.
  2. Find your NCP for your theme in the NCP directory and save their e-mail address now, before you have a question.
  3. Put a reminder in your calendar 48 hours before your call deadline as a "submit by" date, in line with the Online Manual advice.

If you'd rather not do it yourself:

  • National Contact Points: free (as of October 2026; check the official page). They suit first-time applicants who want advice on eligibility and fit in their own language. They are not for anyone who wants their proposal written, and they cannot fix portal bugs.
  • Research Enquiry Service: free (as of October 2026; check the official page). It suits consultants and research offices with precise legal or financial questions about Horizon Europe. It isn't built for urgent technical fixes on deadline day.
  • Private grant consultants: paid, and priced by quote. Fees vary widely by scope and many combine a fixed fee with a success fee, so ask for a written quote (prices change; check with each provider). They suit teams with no time or experience, or ones applying to competitive calls such as the EIC. They are not for applicants who only have a technical portal problem, which the free IT Helpdesk handles. A consultant also can't get you faster IT support than you could get yourself.

Related guides on this site:

FAQ

Is the EU Funding and Tenders Portal Helpdesk free to use?

Yes. The IT Helpdesk is a European Commission service reached through a free online form. NCPs and the Research Enquiry Service are free too. You only pay if you choose to hire a private consultant.

Can you contact the helpdesk by phone instead of a ticket?

The contact form is the documented main channel. A phone number (+32 2 29 92222) and the e-mail address EC-FUNDING-TENDER-SERVICE-DESK@ec.europa.eu appear in the Commission's SEP evaluation quick guide for technical SEP issues (SEP Expert Evaluation guide). Even if you call, open a written ticket as well, because complaints depend on a written record.

What is the difference between the IT Helpdesk and the Research Enquiry Service?

The IT Helpdesk handles IT-related questions about portal tools, such as submission errors, registration forms and login problems. The Research Enquiry Service answers questions about research programmes and funding instruments, including legal and financial points for Horizon Europe (R&I Contact us).

Do you need an EU Login account to submit a helpdesk ticket?

The documented route to the IT Helpdesk is through the portal, and the form is easiest to reach once you are logged in through the user icon. If EU Login itself is the problem, start with the EU Login help FAQ. The Guidance & documents > Helpdesk & support menu can be opened without logging in.

item.title: Horizon Europe Health Calls 2027: 17 Topics, Dates, Budgets
item.dc:creator: Aoba Works
item.description: Horizon Europe health calls 2027: all 17 Cluster 1 topics in one table with budgets, 17 Feb and 16 Sep 2027 deadlines, page limits and steps to apply.
item.content:encoded:
How this guide was made: drafted with AI assistance from the official sources linked below, then passed an automated editorial check before publishing. Our process

The 2027 Horizon Europe Health calls have 17 Cluster 1 topics split across three calls. Two of them, HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01 (single-stage) and HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-two-stage, open on 29 October 2026 and close on 17 February 2027. The third, HORIZON-HLTH-2027-03, opens on 3 June 2027 and closes on 16 September 2027 (Accelopment summary of the Work Programme; Innovate UK Business Connect). The indicative budget is about EUR 609.7 million across roughly 75 projects. All 17 topics are listed below, so you can compare them before you settle on one topic page.

Which option is right for you?

Choose your call based on how much time you have before the deadline and what your team can actually deliver. As of 25 October 2026, the February deadline is less than four months away.

Your situationWhat to pick firstFirst page to open
First-time applicant, no consortium yetHORIZON-HLTH-2027-03 (16 Sep 2027). It gives you the most time to build a partnershipFunding & Tenders Portal topic search, filtered to "Forthcoming"
Consortium already formed, full proposal can be written by mid-FebruaryA HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01 single-stage topic. You get one decision, with no second roundTopic page of your chosen 2027-01 topic, then the "Start submission" area
Good idea, but your partners aren't confirmedA HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-two-stage topic. Stage 1 is only 10 pages/horizon-hlth-2027-02-tool-01-two-stage-dates-page-limits/ as a worked example
SME with a product near market (diagnostics, devices)HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-IND-02-two-stage (Innovation Action)The IND-02 topic page. Also compare /eu-funding-for-smes-7-open-2026-calls-and-how-to-qualify/
Small team, small budget, policy or community focusHORIZON-HLTH-2027-03-TOOL-08 (CSA, EUR 2.9 million, one project)TOOL-08 topic page
Solo startup with no wish to join a consortiumHealth calls are a poor fit. Look at the EIC Accelerator instead/eic-accelerator-deadlines-2026-cut-off-dates-and-steps/

These picks follow from the deadlines and action types in the tables below. The two-stage route takes less writing up front, but you wait until the 16 September 2027 stage 2 deadline before you know the final result.

What Horizon Europe Health Calls Are Open for 2027?

There are 17 Health topics with 2027 deadlines. Ten sit in HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01, four in HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-two-stage and three in HORIZON-HLTH-2027-03. The list and budgets below come from the Work Programme as summarised by Accelopment, which reports the updated programme was published on 1 October 2026. The European Health and Digital Executive Agency (HaDEA) runs the Cluster 1 Health calls.

The topic budgets add up to the call totals reported for the updated programme: EUR 341.6 million for 2027-01, EUR 186.6 million for the two-stage call and EUR 81.5 million for 2027-03 (Accelopment, draft changes).

Watch out for these:

  • Old deadlines on third-party pages. Some institutional pages still give 13 April 2027 as the deadline and 8 May 2026 as the opening date (IRSJD announcement). Those were the draft dates. The amended programme moved stage 1 and the 2027-01 deadline to 17 February 2027 (Accelopment). Go by the portal topic page.
  • The AI topic was renamed. TOOL-08 was first called "Towards the next generation of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) for healthcare". It is now "Towards the next generation of frontier Artificial Intelligence models for healthcare", and the budget is still EUR 2.9 million (Accelopment). If you search for the old name, you may not find it.
  • Deadlines can move. The Work Programme lets the responsible Director-General delay deadlines by up to two months (Innovate UK Business Connect). Check the "Topic updates" tab now and then.

How to Find the Full List of Horizon Europe Health Topics

Search the Funding & Tenders Portal by call identifier and status. Don't rely on a single linked topic page. A search for the "HORIZON-HLTH-2027" prefix brings back all 17 topics in one list.

  1. Open the Funding & Tenders Portal topic search. You don't need to log in to browse.
  2. In the search box, type HORIZON-HLTH-2027. Each topic ID starts with this prefix, so the results include all three calls.
  3. Under Submission status, tick Forthcoming and Open For Submission. Until 29 October 2026, the 2027-01 and 2027-02 topics show as Forthcoming. After that date they show as Open. The 2027-03 topics stay Forthcoming until 3 June 2027.
  4. Under Programme, choose Horizon Europe (HORIZON) to remove calls from other programmes that mention health.
  5. Sort by deadline. Then open each topic and read the Topic description (Expected Outcome, Scope, Type of Action) and the Topic updates tab.
  6. If you want the full context, download the Health Work Programme itself (Work Programme 2026-2027, part 4 Health, PDF). It gives the destination introductions that topic pages leave out.

For example, say you work on wearable diagnostics. A keyword search for "diagnostics" might only show IND-02. A prefix search also brings up TOOL-01 (AI biomarkers) and CARE-02 (adverse drug reactions), and your work may fit those better.

If the portal isn't loading results, it is usually a session issue rather than an empty list. Log out, clear filters, and search again. If you need to log in for the submission steps later, see /eu-funding-and-tenders-portal-two-factor-authentication-2026/.

What Are the Deadlines for Horizon Europe Health Calls 2027?

There are two 2027 Health deadline dates: 17 February 2027 and 16 September 2027, both at 17:00:00 Brussels time. Which one applies depends on whether your topic is single-stage or two-stage (Innovate UK Business Connect).

CallProcessOpensDeadline 1Deadline 2Topics
HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01Single-stage29 Oct 202617 Feb 2027—10
HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-two-stageTwo-stage29 Oct 202617 Feb 2027 (stage 1, short proposal)16 Sep 2027 (stage 2, full proposal)4
HORIZON-HLTH-2027-03Single-stage3 Jun 202716 Sep 2027—3

The dates changed between the draft and the final text. The two-stage call originally had a stage 1 deadline of 13 April 2027 and an opening date of 10 February 2027. Call 2027-03 was originally due on 22 September 2027 (Accelopment). So the February calls are open for about 16 weeks, not the five or so months many teams expected.

In a two-stage call, only proposals that pass stage 1 are invited to write the full proposal. The Horizon Europe General Annexes explain how stage 1 is scored. It covers excellence and impact, not implementation. Stage 1 of the 2027 two-stage call also uses blind evaluation, so parts of the short proposal must be anonymised (FFG overview, cited in search results).

Common deadline mistakes and how to fix them:

  • Submitting at 16:55 Brussels time. The submission system closes at the deadline and does not accept proposals after it, and the Commission advises applicants not to wait until the last moment (Funding & Tenders Portal Online Manual). Aim to submit a complete version 48 hours early. You can keep replacing it until the deadline, because only the last version counts.
  • Converting time zones wrong. 17:00 Brussels is CET in February and CEST in September. If you are in the UK, that is 16:00 local time on both dates.
  • Breaking anonymity in stage 1. Partner names in file metadata, logos in figures, or phrases like "our previous project X" can all identify you. Strip the PDF metadata and refer to earlier work in the third person.

Horizon Europe Health Calls 2027 vs 2026: What's Different?

The 2027 Health calls are a little bigger and spread over three deadlines. 2026 had one main single-stage deadline. Both years use the same six destinations.

Feature2026 Health calls2027 Health calls
Main call(s)HORIZON-HLTH-2026-01 (single-stage)2027-01 (single), 2027-02-two-stage, 2027-03 (single)
Main deadline16 April 2026, 17:00 CET (HaDEA)17 Feb 2027 and 16 Sep 2027
Topics17 in HLTH-2026-01 (HaDEA)17 across three calls
Expected projects68 (Accelopment)About 75 (Accelopment)
Two-stage optionNone in the 2026 main call (the 2025 two-stage call closed stage 2 on 16 April 2026)Four topics
Indicative totalNot stated in the HaDEA noticeAbout EUR 609.7M

The topics also lean in a different direction. In 2026, HaDEA's destination split was 2 topics for Staying healthy, 3 for Environment, 6 for Diseases, 2 for Care access, 4 for Tools and 1 for Industry. In 2027 there are 1, 2, 6, 1, 4 and 2 respectively, counted from the topic list above. In 2027, the Diseases destination puts more weight on infectious disease: two monoclonal-antibody topics, small-molecule antivirals and antimicrobials. The Tools destination adds bio-printing, Virtual Human Twins and frontier AI.

If you missed the 2026 deadline and are reusing that proposal, check the scope text line by line. A 2026 topic with a similar title may have a different Expected Outcome in 2027. The 2026-2027 Part B template also shortened the page limits (see the next section).

What Is the Page Limit for Horizon Europe Health Proposals?

Under the 2026-2027 Work Programme, a full Health proposal is limited to 40 pages for RIA and IA, 25 pages for CSA, and 10 pages for a two-stage stage 1 proposal. Lump-sum topics are allowed 45 pages (RIA/IA) and 28 pages (CSA) (General Annexes 2026-2027).

Proposal typePage limit 2026-2027Older 2021-2022 limit, for comparison
RIA / IA, full proposal4045
CSA, full proposal2530

CSA, lump sum28—

The older figures come from the 2021-2022 General Annexes. Many online guides still say 45/30 or 45/70. Those numbers are out of date for 2027 topics.

How to apply this to the table of 17 topics:

  • The ten 2027-01 RIA topics and the 2027-03 RIA topics (TOOL-02, TOOL-04): 40 pages, or 45 if the topic page says lump sum.
  • TOOL-08 (CSA): 25 pages, or 28 if lump sum.
  • The four two-stage topics: 10 pages at stage 1, then 40 (or 45 for lump sum) at stage 2.
  • ENVHLTH-MISSCLIMA-03 (PCP): open the Part B template attached to the topic. PCP actions have a dedicated application form, listed separately from the RIA/IA form in the portal's reference documents.

The template version changed too. Version 5.0, dated 5 November 2025, shortened sections 2.1 and 3.1 (Criteri summary). Always use the Part B template you get from that topic's submission system, not a copy from an earlier proposal. For how the sections map to evaluator scores, see /horizon-europe-proposal-template-part-b-2026-scoring-map/.

Mistakes that come up often:

  • Thinking annexes don't count. According to the standard application form, excess pages in an over-long proposal are automatically made invisible after the deadline and are not taken into account by the experts (Standard Application Form, HE RIA/IA). The cover page, table of contents and Part A forms don't count. Everything inside Part B sections 1 to 3 does.
  • Squeezing the layout. The template sets a minimum font size and minimum margins (Standard Application Form, HE RIA/IA). Shrinking them to fit more text breaks the formatting rules.
  • Treating "no page limit" as a real option. Every Health topic uses a capped Part B. The only difference is which cap applies.

Who Can Apply to Horizon Europe Health Calls?

For RIA and IA Health topics, you need at least three independent legal entities. At least one must be in an EU Member State, and at least two others must be in different Member States or Associated Countries (IRSJD summary of the conditions; General Annexes). Universities, SMEs, hospitals, NGOs and public bodies all count as legal entities.

The country rules for Cluster 1 are broader than most people expect:

  • Associated Countries apply on the same terms as Member States. Switzerland has been fully associated from 2025 calls onwards. Canada and the Republic of Korea are associated to Pillar II, which includes Cluster 1 Health (Kronis summary; Science|Business).
  • United States. The Health Work Programme says legal entities established in the US can receive Union funding in the Health Cluster. The reason given is that the US National Institutes of Health opened its programmes to European researchers (Health Work Programme 2026-2027). A US partner still can't replace one of the three required EU or associated entities.
  • Low- and middle-income countries listed in the General Annexes are generally eligible for funding. Other non-associated countries can take part, but they usually pay their own way.
  • CSA topics such as TOOL-08 can have a lower minimum, often a single entity, depending on the topic conditions. Check the "Eligibility" section of the topic page.

Health calls are not set aside for SMEs. A startup can lead a consortium, but there is no SME-only Health route in 2027. If you want to apply alone, the EIC is the place to look.

Checking eligibility in three steps:

  1. List your partners with their country of establishment, not the nationality of the researcher.
  2. Check that at least one partner is in an EU Member State and that the three required partners are in three different countries.
  3. Read the topic page for any extra conditions, such as clinical trial requirements or restrictions on participation.

For example, a consortium of a German university, a Spanish hospital and a Swiss SME meets the minimum. A Dutch startup plus a US hospital does not, because only one partner is in a Member State or Associated Country.

The most common problem is that a partner's PIC isn't validated. Validation can take weeks, so register early. /eu-funding-and-tenders-portal-registration-pic-in-6-steps/ walks through it.

How Much Funding Can You Get from a Horizon Europe Health Call?

A typical 2027 Health RIA project receives between EUR 3 million and EUR 12 million from the EU. The CSA (TOOL-08) gets EUR 2.9 million, and the PCP topic gets EUR 4–5 million per project (Accelopment). Under Horizon Europe, RIA and CSA cover 100% of eligible costs. IA covers 70%, rising to 100% for non-profit entities (General Annexes).

Range per projectTopicsRoughly how many grants per topic
Under EUR 5MDISEASE-10 (EUR 3–4M), MISSCLIMA-03 PCP (EUR 4–5M), TOOL-08 CSA (EUR 2.9M)3–4; 4–5; 1

The grant counts are estimates: topic budget divided by the per-project range. For example, DISEASE-01 has EUR 63.8M and EUR 7–8M per project, which suggests about 8 grants. TOOL-08 funds exactly one. HaDEA can fund fewer projects than this if the proposals aren't strong enough.

Here is how the funding rate works for a point-of-care device project under IND-02, an Innovation Action. Say an SME partner has EUR 1,000,000 of eligible costs. It would receive EUR 700,000. A university partner in the same consortium with the same costs would receive EUR 1,000,000. A request that falls outside the stated range isn't automatically ineligible, but evaluators will expect a good reason for it.

How to Apply for a Horizon Europe Health Call (Step by Step)

You apply on the Funding & Tenders Portal. Create an EU Login, get a PIC for each partner, start a draft from the topic page, and submit before 17:00 Brussels time on the deadline.

  1. Create an EU Login account from the portal's Login button, and set up two-factor authentication.
  2. Register or find your organisation's PIC under Participant Register. Each partner needs its own PIC (PIC guide).
  3. Pick your topic using the table above, then confirm the scope on the topic page.
  4. Agree the consortium and roles. The coordinator starts the submission. Partners are added by PIC and contact email.
  5. On the topic page, scroll to "Start submission", choose the type of action and form, enter the coordinator's PIC and create the draft.
  6. Fill in Part A online (administrative forms and budget table). Upload Part B using the template downloaded from that draft.
  7. Run "Validate" to catch missing fields or an over-length Part B. Then click "Submit". Track the status under My Proposals (status guide).

Pitfalls and fixes:

  • Only the coordinator's contacts can submit. Partner contacts can edit the draft but can't press Submit, which is reserved for the coordinator organisation's contacts (Funding & Tenders Portal Online Manual). Have the Primary Coordinator Contact add a backup Coordinator Contact in case they are unavailable on deadline day.
  • Budget mismatches between Part A and Part B. Lock the budget table a week before the deadline and update both parts together.
  • Ethics self-assessment left until the end. Health topics often involve human data or clinical work. Fill in the ethics section of Part A early.
  • Stage 2 surprises. Your stage 2 proposal can't stray far from the stage 1 version. If you change partners or scope significantly, evaluators may notice.

Next steps

You have four days until the 2027-01 and 2027-02 calls open, so today is a good day to shortlist topics and check partner PICs.

DIY actions for today:

  1. Run the HORIZON-HLTH-2027 search on the topic search page and shortlist no more than three topics from the table above.
  2. Check that each likely partner has a validated PIC. If they don't, start registration now.
  3. Write down your deadline plan: 17 Feb 2027 single-stage, 17 Feb plus 16 Sep 2027 two-stage, or 16 Sep 2027 for 2027-03.

If you'd rather not do it alone:

  • National Contact Points (NCPs) give free advice and partner-search help in every Member State and Associated Country. You can find them via the portal's NCP directory. This suits first-time applicants and universities. It doesn't suit anyone looking for someone to write the proposal, because NCPs advise but don't draft.
  • Enterprise Europe Network (EEN) offers free support to SMEs, including partner search (EEN). It is a good fit for startups looking for academic partners. Its limitation is that advisers vary in how well they know health topics.
  • Private grant consultants can write and manage the proposal for you. Fees vary and are often a mix of a fixed fee and a success fee (as of October 2026; ask for a written quote). This works best for SMEs without in-house grant experience. It's a poor fit for teams that can't afford to pay if the proposal is rejected, and no consultant can guarantee success.

FAQ

2027 horizon europe health calls for proposals: how many are there?

There are three calls (HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01, HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-two-stage and HORIZON-HLTH-2027-03) covering 17 topics. Together they have an indicative budget of about EUR 609.7 million and are expected to fund roughly 75 projects (Accelopment).

Horizon Europe health calls: who manages them?

HaDEA, the European Health and Digital Executive Agency, runs the Cluster 1 Health calls for the European Commission (HaDEA). You submit and track proposals on the Funding & Tenders Portal.

When does the Horizon Europe Health Work Programme 2027 open?

The 2027-01 and 2027-02-two-stage calls open on 29 October 2026. The 2027-03 call opens on 3 June 2027 (Innovate UK Business Connect). Pages that still list 8 May 2026 as the opening date are showing old draft dates.

Is there a Horizon Europe Health call with no page limit?

No. Every 2027 Health topic caps Part B. The limits are 40 pages for RIA/IA, 25 for CSA and 10 for stage 1, or 45 and 28 for lump-sum topics (General Annexes). Evaluators ignore any pages over the limit (Standard Application Form, HE RIA/IA).

Can non-EU organisations apply to Horizon Europe Health calls?

Yes. Entities in Associated Countries such as Switzerland, Canada and Korea take part on the same terms as EU members. US entities can receive funding in the Health Cluster specifically (Health Work Programme). The consortium must still include at least one Member State entity and meet the three-country minimum.
